description: Agriculture is a constant dance between climate, soil, and human effort. NISAR AgroView follows the beat of that dance from orbit using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data, giving a visual voice to agricultural land changes and building accessible tools for a more sustainable farming future.
summary:
The NISAR AgroView is a live/real time agriculture monitoring and crop health validation platform that uses the NASA ISRO SAR (NISAR) level 2 radar data.

To address this issue of the sheer volume of satellite data downloaded; NISAR Agroview streams the polarimetric GCOV granules directly from NASA Earth Data cloud through HTTP 206 Range Request to each user's browser.

For any field polygon drawn by users on the map; The NISAR Agro View extracts only the portion of the GCOV granule associated with the target area into memory to calculate the Radar Vegetation Index (RVI) and Backscattering Differentials in a matter of seconds; No Local Storage Required.

This is important because radar can penetrate clouds, smoke and darkness in areas where optical imagery cannot; Therefore, the NISAR Agro View provides instantaneous, all weather crop health insight and damage assessments.
details:
NISAR AgroView is a cloud-native platform for on-demand agricultural monitoring using NASA-ISRO SAR (NISAR) Level-2 radar data.

  • How it works & Creativity: Instead of downloading massive GB files, it streams only the user-selected farm polygon directly from NASA Earthdata Cloud via HTTP 206 byte-range requests, computing radar analytics in-memory with zero local disk storage.
  • Benefits & Impact: L-band radar penetrates clouds, haze, and darkness where optical satellites fail. By slashing data transfer by 99% (streaming ~40 MB in 13s), it democratizes instant crop health (RVI), harvest tracking, and flood assessment for farmers and agronomists worldwide.
  • Tools Used: Python (h5py, numpy, pyproj), NASA CMR & ASF APIs, Leaflet.js, Chart.js, Docker.
  • Factors Considered: Bandwidth limits in rural areas, NISAR’s 12-day orbit cycle, and making radar data accessible to non-GIS experts.
